rationale: This benchmark is tiny (6 functions, ~1.4 KB of text) but loop-hot: update_crc runs per packet byte and gen_crc_table iterates 256 times, so runtime-cost weights are kept low across all passes to steer application away from the hottest code while SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights as a near-free, correctness-safe baseline that obscures arithmetic (CRC XOR/add patterns) everywhere. FLA and IBR receive the next-highest benefit weights because control-flow flattening and indirect branching give the strongest structural resistance in small binaries where a reversing engineer can otherwise trivially diff the control-flow graph, and their moderate (0.2-0.3) cost weights let the selector apply them to the larger, less-hot functions (main, gen_crc_table) rather than the per-byte loop. BCF is moderated (0.6/0.5) because its size and runtime bloat is disproportionate on a 1.4 KB binary with tight loops, and SPLIT is dampened (0.4/0.4) since the functions are already very small, leaving little to split. ICALL is the weakest fit because the call graph has only ~6 nodes, so converting direct calls to indirect ones buys little diversity for real dispatch overhead, while IGV is kept mid-range because the 10k-entry packet_lengths table makes global-reference indirection one of the few genuinely valuable targets in this program. CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.2 throughout to preserve functional equivalence of the CRC computation.
